subject.title: Feature Request: Support message recall/edit events to cancel running tasks

question: Should OpenClaw define a shared source-message lifecycle contract for channel edit/delete/recall events, or keep this behavior as channel-specific plugin logic for now?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent behavior affects session state, channel delivery semantics, plugin API boundaries, and potentially user-visible cancellation defaults across multiple channels.

options.title: Define shared lifecycle contract
options.body: Add a narrow core/plugin contract for source-message edit/delete/recall events and require channels to map native events into that contract before cancelling or superseding runs.

options.title: Land channel slices only
options.body: Handle each supported channel independently and accept some duplicated semantics until a repeated pattern justifies a shared contract.

options.title: Defer until one channel proves it live
options.body: Keep this umbrella open but wait for a proof-positive channel PR to establish the minimal behavior before committing to cross-channel API shape.

recommendation.title: Define shared lifecycle contract
recommendation.body: Add a narrow core/plugin contract for source-message edit/delete/recall events and require channels to map native events into that contract before cancelling or superseding runs.

likelyOwner.reason: The likely decision touches the channel/plugin architecture and shared inbound context surfaces where this person has the clearest recent history.
